text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'A separate XGBoost model predicts power for each wind meter using the input set labelled on each row. The forecasting method, XGBoost, combines decision trees trained to reduce squared prediction errors. All XGBoost models use the corrected wind and radiation processing. A means training April 2024–June 2025 and scoring July 2025–June 2026. B means training July 2025–June 2026 and scoring April 2024–June 2025, and is retrospective. Lean wind retains 16 of the full control’s 24 real inputs, removing selected weather and calendar inputs. All scored forecast times are included. Each row shows forecast error with lean inputs minus forecast error with full inputs under the labelled conditions. Each decision tree ends in leaves, which supply prediction values. Tree depth limits successive splits; learning rate controls each update’s size. Minimum child weight limits small leaves; the L2 penalty discourages large fitted leaf values. Main uses 500 trees, maximum depth 6, learning rate 0.05, minimum child weight 1, and L2 penalty 1. Sensitivity, labelled alt, uses 1200 trees, maximum depth 4, learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, and L2 penalty 5. Both training settings sample 80% of training rows per tree and allow all input columns. Padded rows duplicate retained inputs to keep 24 training columns. Unpadded rows use the 16 lean or 24 full real inputs without duplicates. Ordinary rows use the original windchill formula. Guarded rows use that formula only at temperatures at most 10°C and 10 m wind speeds at least 4.8 km/h; otherwise windchill equals air temperature. Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative weather prediction supplied by the weather ensemble. Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is better. Fair CRPS adjusts for the finite number of forecast values, assuming independent samples from the forecast distribution. That assumption is not established for these weather-ensemble values; the corrected score is a diagnostic comparison. Each row uses matched forecasts and observations and weights wind meters and three random-seed fits equally. A seed sets a training run’s random choices. Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or transfer to new meters. These separate loss contrasts do not directly test differences between the guard, training-setting, or padding effects and establish no causal mechanism. Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Each forecast loss is divided by its meter’s capacity and expressed as a percentage before averaging meters. Capacity is used only for scoring. Each interval draw resamples whole months and selects one training seed shared by the lean and full XGBoost models. Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one matched training seed. Negative differences mean lower loss with lean wind inputs; positive differences mean higher loss. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
text.tspan: A separate XGBoost model predicts power for each wind meter using the input set labelled on each row.
The forecasting method, XGBoost, combines decision trees trained to reduce squared prediction errors.
All XGBoost models use the corrected wind and radiation processing.
A means training April 2024–June 2025 and scoring July 2025–June 2026. B means training July 2025–June 2026 and
scoring April 2024–June 2025, and is retrospective.
Lean wind retains 16 of the full control’s 24 real inputs, removing selected weather and calendar inputs.
All scored forecast times are included. Each row shows forecast error with lean inputs minus forecast error with
full inputs under the labelled conditions.
Each decision tree ends in leaves, which supply prediction values. Tree depth limits successive splits; learning
rate controls each update’s size. Minimum child weight limits small leaves; the L2 penalty discourages large fitted
leaf values.
Main uses 500 trees, maximum depth 6, learning rate 0.05, minimum child weight 1, and L2 penalty 1.
Sensitivity, labelled alt, uses 1200 trees, maximum depth 4, learning rate 0.03, minimum child weight 50, and L2
penalty 5.
Both training settings sample 80% of training rows per tree and allow all input columns.
Padded rows duplicate retained inputs to keep 24 training columns. Unpadded rows use the 16 lean or 24 full real
inputs without duplicates.
Ordinary rows use the original windchill formula. Guarded rows use that formula only at temperatures at most 10°C
and 10 m wind speeds at least 4.8 km/h; otherwise windchill equals air temperature.
Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative weather prediction supplied by the weather
ensemble.
Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is
better.
Fair CRPS adjusts for the finite number of forecast values, assuming independent samples from the forecast
distribution. That assumption is not established for these weather-ensemble values; the corrected score is a
diagnostic comparison.
Each row uses matched forecasts and observations and weights wind meters and three random-seed fits equally. A seed
sets a training run’s random choices.
Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or
transfer to new meters.
These separate loss contrasts do not directly test differences between the guard, training-setting, or padding
effects and establish no causal mechanism.
Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Each
forecast loss is divided by its meter’s capacity and expressed as a percentage before averaging meters. Capacity is
used only for scoring.
Each interval draw resamples whole months and selects one training seed shared by the lean and full XGBoost models.
Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one
matched training seed.
Negative differences mean lower loss with lean wind inputs; positive differences mean higher loss.
All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.
